mainTopic: Honest scales, weights and measures: building rules, materials, leveling, the פסוק in ויקרא, and the ban on keeping wrong measures
overview: This amud is all about honest scales, weights and measures. רב פפא explains a word from the earlier ברייתא about scales. רבי מני בר פטיש then teaches that the building rules for scales also decide when their parts become טמא. The גמרא shows that this adds something the משנה in כלים does not cover: the beam and its cord. A series of ברייתות follows. Weights may not be made of metal, and the leveler must be made of medium-weight wood, be even on both sides, and be used at a normal pace. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי worried that teaching these rules might help cheaters, but he taught them anyway, relying on a פסוק in הושע. A ברייתא then explains the honest-measure פסוק in ויקרא and uses a קל וחומר to show that every measure must be honest. Finally, רב forbids keeping a wrong-sized measure at home. The גמרא rejects רב פפא's exceptions and supports רב with a ברייתא whose list of proper measures continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא explains a word: a blacksmiths' scale
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that a term in the earlier ברייתא means a scale used by blacksmiths.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: It means a blacksmiths' scale.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is explaining a word from the ברייתא we just learned about how different kinds of scales must be built. He says it refers to a heavy-duty scale used by blacksmiths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave different building rules for different kinds of scales. רב פפא tells us which real-life scale one of those types is: the kind blacksmiths use to weigh heavy pieces of metal. Knowing the type of scale helps us understand why its rule is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Blacksmiths, metalworkers; here, a scale used by them

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Blacksmiths.
phrases.notes: He means the scale in the ברייתא is a blacksmiths' scale, built for weighing heavy metal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a term from the ברייתא discussed just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The term in the ברייתא refers to a blacksmiths' scale.

steps.title: The building rules for scales also apply to their טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני בר פטיש says the same rules that govern how scales must be built for honest use also decide when their parts become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני בר פטיש says: Just as the חכמים said these rules regarding what is forbidden, so they said them regarding טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני בר פטיש takes the rules about how a scale must be built and applies them to a second area: טומאה. Whatever counts as a proper part of the scale for honest weighing also counts as part of the scale for becoming טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא taught how long the ropes and parts of a scale must be, so that using a scale built differently is forbidden. רבי מני בר פטיש adds that these same measurements decide whether the ropes and parts are treated as part of the כלי for טומאה. If they are not attached in the proper way, they do not become טמא as part of the scale.

keyTerms.meaning: Their prohibition: the rule that using an improperly built scale is forbidden
Their ritual impurity: whether the scale's parts can become טמא

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani bar Pattish says:
Just as they said regarding their prohibition,
phrases.notes: "Their" means the scales. These are the building rules from the ברייתא that make an improper scale forbidden to use.

phrases.english: so they said regarding their ritual impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same ברייתא about scales, carrying its rules over into the laws of טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The required measurements of a scale's parts for honest use also decide whether those parts count as part of the scale for טומאה.

steps.title: Why say it? A משנה already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מני בר פטיש adds, since a משנה already says the rope of a storekeeper's or homeowner's scale must be one טפח to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in a משנה: The rope of the scales of a storekeeper or of homeowners must be one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מני בר פטיש: his teaching seems unnecessary, because a משנה already connects the length of a scale's rope to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in כלים says the rope of a regular scale becomes טמא together with the scale when it is a טפח long. That already seems to show that the measurements of a scale matter for טומאה. So what new thing is רבי מני בר פטיש telling us?

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? The question used when a teaching seems to add nothing new
A handbreadth, a unit of measure

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in כלים 29:5.

phrases.english: The rope of the scales of a storekeeper
and of homeowners – one handbreadth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of רבי מני בר פטיש as already known from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement of רבי מני בר פטיש in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in כלים already links a scale's rope measurement to טומאה, so his statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: He was needed for the beam and its cord
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה only covers the hanging rope; רבי מני בר פטיש teaches the rule for the beam and its cord, which the משנה does not mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed to teach about the beam and its cord, which we did not learn in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the משנה only talks about one part of the scale, the rope the pans hang from. רבי מני בר פטיש is needed to teach the same rule for other parts, the beam and its cord.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה covers just the rope. Without רבי מני בר פטיש, we would not know whether the beam and its cord also follow the building measurements for טומאה. His general statement fills that gap, so it is not extra after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A cord, the cord the beam hangs from
It was necessary for him to teach this

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה only gives the טומאה rule for the hanging rope of a scale. רבי מני בר פטיש extends it to the beam and its cord: all parts follow the same building measurements for טומאה.

phrases.english: The beam and its cord
were necessary for him to teach,
since we did not learn them in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by showing what new parts רבי מני בר פטיש covers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the earlier source: the משנה covers only the rope, so the new teaching adds the beam and cord.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His statement seemed to repeat what the משנה already teaches about the rope.
steps.terutzMaskana: His statement is needed to apply the טומאה rule to the beam and its cord, which the משנה never mentions.

steps.title: Which materials may be used to make weights
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that weights may not be made of tin, lead, an alloy, or any other metal, but may be made of hard stone or glass.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One may not make weights of tin, lead, alloy, or any other kind of metal. But one may make them of hard stone or of glass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about weights. It lists which materials are forbidden for making weights and which are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All kinds of metal are forbidden for weights, while hard stone and glass are allowed. The usual explanation is that metal wears away over time, so the weight gets lighter and the buyer pays for more than he gets. Hard stone and glass keep their weight, so they stay honest.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that honesty in business is not only about how you weigh, but also about choosing tools that will stay accurate over time.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may not make weights –

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שֶׁל בַּעַץ, וְלֹא שֶׁל אֲבָר,
phrases.english: not of tin, and not of lead,
and not of metal alloy,
and not of any other kinds of metal.
But one may make them
of hard rock and of glass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the building of scales to the materials used for weights, staying within the topic of honest measures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weights may not be made of any metal; they may be made of hard stone or glass.

steps.title: What material a leveler may be made of
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that the leveler may not be made of gourd, which is too light, or of metal, which is too heavy. It must be made of medium-weight woods.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: You may not make a leveler from gourd, because it is too light. You may not make it from metal, because it is too heavy. But you may make it from olive wood, nut wood, sycamore wood, or boxwood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the stick used to sweep extra grain off the top of a measuring vessel. It tells us which materials are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A light leveler leaves too much grain on top, so the seller loses. A heavy one presses down and scoops out too much, so the buyer loses. Medium-weight wood is fair to both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: A leveler: a flat stick that sweeps extra grain off the rim of a measuring vessel
Gourd: a light, hollow plant material
Heavy; it presses down too hard

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not make the leveler out of gourd
phrases.notes: The leveler is the stick you run across the top of a full measure, so the buyer gets exactly a level measure.

phrases.english: because it is light,
and not out of metal,
because it is heavy.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹשֵׂהוּ שֶׁל זַיִת וְשֶׁל אֱגוֹז,
phrases.english: But one may make it out of olive wood or nut wood,
or out of sycamore or boxwood.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין עוֹשִׂין הַמֶּחָק שֶׁל דְּלַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rules for honest measuring tools. Step 5 dealt with weights; this step deals with the leveler.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leveler must be made of medium-weight wood, not gourd and not metal.

steps.title: The leveler's shape and how to level fairly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that the leveler must be even on both sides. It also says one may not level in one quick sweep or in many slow little strokes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: You may not make a leveler that is thick on one side and thin on the other. Do not level in one quick sweep, because that hurts the seller and helps the buyer. Do not level little by little, because that hurts the buyer and helps the seller.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא adds rules about the leveler's shape and about the way a person uses it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stick that is thick on one side and thin on the other would not level evenly. One fast sweep leaves extra grain behind, which is good for the buyer. Many slow strokes scrape away too much, which is good for the seller. The rule demands one normal, fair motion.

keyTerms.meaning: All at once, in one quick motion

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not make the leveler

phrases.aramaic: צִדּוֹ אֶחָד עָב וְצִדּוֹ אֶחָד קָצָר.
phrases.english: with one side thick and the other side thin.
One should not level all at once,
because leveling all at once
is bad for the seller and good for the buyer;
and one should not level little by little,
because it is bad for the buyer and good for the seller.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין עוֹשִׂין אֶת הַמֶּחָק צִדּוֹ אֶחָד עָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more rules about the same leveler from step 6, now about its shape and how it is used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leveler must be even, and leveling must be done at a normal pace, neither in one quick sweep nor in many slow strokes.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's dilemma about teaching these rules
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says he is caught either way. Teaching these rules might teach cheaters new tricks, but staying silent might make cheaters think the חכמים don't understand their methods.
steps.simpleTranslation: About all these rules, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: Woe to me if I say them, and woe to me if I don't. If I say them, cheaters might learn new tricks. If I don't, cheaters might say: "Torah scholars don't understand how we work."
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי shares a worry about all the measuring rules just taught. Explaining the rules also means explaining the tricks they forbid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each option carries a risk. Teaching the rules reveals the cheating methods to people who did not know them. Silence lets cheaters believe the חכמים are naive, so they will feel free to cheat without fear.

keyTerms.meaning: Our handiwork, meaning the cheaters' methods

phrases.aramaic: עַל כּוּלָּן אָמַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: About all of these, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said:
Woe to me if I say them,
woe to me if I do not say them;
if I say them, perhaps the cheaters will learn,
and if I do not say them,
perhaps the cheaters will say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בְּקִיאִין בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ.
phrases.english: Torah scholars are not experts in our handiwork.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כּוּלָּן אָמַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reflects on all the measuring rules just taught and on whether they should be taught at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching the anti-cheating rules carries a risk whether one teaches them or stays silent.

steps.title: Did he end up teaching the rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבן יוחנן בן זכאי finally decided to teach these rules or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question was asked: Did he say them, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a question about how רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's dilemma ended. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 laid out both risks but did not tell us his decision. This question looks for the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was asked of them": the חכמים raised a question

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Did he say it, or did he not say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: אַמְרַהּ, אוֹ לָא אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the dilemma in step 8 was resolved.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבן יוחנן בן זכאי actually taught the measuring rules in public.

steps.title: He taught them, based on a פסוק in הושע
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק answers that he did teach the rules. He relied on the פסוק that says the righteous walk in ה׳'s ways and sinners stumble in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: He said them, and he relied on this פסוק: "For the ways of ה׳ are straight; the righteous walk in them, and sinners stumble in them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי did teach the rules, and the פסוק gave him the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that the same Torah knowledge works differently for different people. Honest people will use the rules to stay honest. If cheaters misuse them, the fault is theirs, so the truth should still be taught.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי taught the anti-cheating rules even though cheaters might misuse them. Honest people walk in the Torah's ways, and if wrongdoers stumble over them, that is their own fault.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
He said it, and he said it based on this verse:
"For the ways of the Lord are straight,
and the righteous walk in them,
but sinners stumble over them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: אַמְרַהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He did teach the rules, relying on the פסוק in הושע that the righteous walk in ה׳'s ways while sinners stumble over them.

steps.title: Explaining measure, weight, and liquid measure in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains three words in the פסוק in ויקרא. Each word points to a specific way of cheating: measuring land in different seasons, keeping weights in salt, and making liquid foam.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: "Do not do wrong in judgment, in measure, in weight, or in liquid measure." "In measure" means measuring land: don't measure for one person in the summer and for another in the rainy season. "In weight" means don't keep your weights in salt. "In liquid measure" means don't make the liquid foam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that explains the honest-measure פסוק in ויקרא word by word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the פסוק is matched to a real trick. A measuring rope gives different results when dry or wet. Salt wears away the weights, so they become too light. Pouring liquid fast fills the measure with foam, so the buyer gets less.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure, here measuring length such as land
Make it foam or bubble up

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the איסור of dishonest measures covers subtle tricks too, even when the tool itself looks honest.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Do not do wrong in judgment,
in measure, in weight, or in liquid measure";
"In measure": this is measuring land,
that one should not measure for one person in the summer
and for another in the rainy season.
"In weight": that one should not hide his weights in salt.
"In liquid measure": that one should not make it foam.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ עָוֶל בַּמִּשְׁפָּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא on the same general subject of honest measures, now explaining the פסוק itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each word of the פסוק forbids a specific trick: uneven land measuring between seasons, salt-worn weights, and foamy liquid measures.

steps.title: If the Torah cares about a tiny measure, surely it cares about all measures
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר: the Torah is strict even about the משורה, which is only one thirty-sixth of a לוג. So it is surely strict about the הין, the לוג, and all the other standard measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here is a קל וחומר. The משורה is only 1/36 of a לוג, and still the Torah was strict about it. So all the more so the Torah is strict about a הין, half a הין, a third and a quarter of a הין, a לוג, half a לוג, a quarter, half a תומן, and an עוכלא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its reading of the פסוק. It uses the word משורה to show that the Torah cares about honesty in every measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 tied the word משורה to a tiny liquid measure. Here the ברייתא reasons that if even something that small matters, then every standard measure must be kept honest. The list of units tells us the rule covers the whole system of measures.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning that if something is true in a lighter case, it is surely true in a heavier case
A tiny liquid measure, 1/36 of a לוג
Was strict about it, cared about it

phrases.english: And it is a קל וחומר:
If a משורה,
phrases.notes: This is the word ובמשורה from the פסוק in ויקרא explained in the step before.

phrases.english: which is one thirty-sixth of a לוג,
the Torah was strict about it;
then all the more so a הין, and a half-הין,
and a third of a הין, and a quarter of a הין;
and a לוג, and a half-לוג, and a quarter,
and a half-תומן, and an עוכלא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 11 by reasoning from the word משורה to all measures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah's demand for honest measuring covers every standard measure, since it even covers the tiny משורה.

steps.title: You may not keep a wrong-sized measure in your house
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person may not keep a measure that is too small or too large at home, even if he only uses it as a chamber pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person may not keep a measure that is too small or too large in his house, even if he uses it as a chamber pot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a new rule. Honesty is not only about how you measure; you may not even own a wrong measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that a wrong measure lying around might one day be used to measure for a customer. That is why even a pot used for something gross, which nobody would think of as a measure, is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure that is too small or too large

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
It is forbidden for a person to keep
a measure that is too small or too large
inside his house,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הִיא עָבִיט שֶׁל מֵימֵי רַגְלַיִם.
phrases.english: and even if it is a chamber pot for urine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָסוּר לָאָדָם שֶׁיַּשְׁהֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from honest measuring to a new rule about owning wrong measures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to keep a wrong-sized measure in one's house, even one used as a chamber pot.

steps.title: רב פפא limits the rule to places with no stamps and no inspectors
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says רב's rule only applies where measures are not stamped. Even there, it only applies where nobody inspects the measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This rule is only for a place where measures are not stamped. Where they are stamped, a buyer who doesn't see the stamp won't take the goods. And even where they are not stamped, the rule is only where nobody inspects measures. If they do inspect, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows רב's rule. He lists two situations where owning a wrong measure would be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that the danger is only real if a wrong measure could actually fool a buyer. If measures carry an official stamp, the buyer checks for it. If inspectors check the measures, a wrong one would be caught. Either way, nobody would be cheated.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in the case of
They are stamped with an official seal
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
We only said this
in a place where measures are not stamped,
but in a place where they are stamped,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא חָזֵי חֲתִימָה לָא שָׁקֵיל.
phrases.english: if he does not see the stamp, he does not take.
phrases.notes: "He" is the buyer. Without seeing the stamp, he won't accept the goods.

phrases.english: And even in a place where they are not stamped,
we only said it where they do not inspect,
but if they do inspect, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּאַתְרָא דְּלָא חֲתִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב's rule from step 13 to certain places only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב פפא, the ban applies only where measures are neither stamped nor inspected.

steps.title: The גמרא rejects the limits: a buyer may not check at twilight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב פפא's limits are wrong. Sometimes a sale happens at twilight, in a rush, and the buyer takes the goods without checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. Sometimes a sale happens at twilight, and the buyer ends up taking the goods without checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא. It says his exceptions do not really protect the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא assumed the stamp or the inspectors would always stop cheating. The גמרא says that in a rushed moment, like at twilight, a buyer may not look for the stamp. So the wrong measure could still be used, and רב's rule stays with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, when it is getting dark

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא's view is the final הלכה. The גמרא rejects it here, so the ban on keeping a wrong measure applies everywhere.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
sometimes it happens at twilight,

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב's rule and lists the measures one may make
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same as רב: no wrong measure at home, even a chamber pot. It then starts listing the proper measures a person may make, from a סאה down to half a תומן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: A person may not keep a measure that is too small or too large in his house, even if it is a chamber pot. But he may make a סאה, a תרקב, half a תרקב, a קב, half a קב, a quarter, a תומן, half a תומן,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב's rule word for word. The ברייתא then begins a list of correct measures that are allowed, and the list continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives רב's rule with no exceptions, which fits the rejection of רב פפא. It also adds a positive side: proper, standard measures may be made and kept. Only wrong-sized ones are banned.
